name: Sync issues from GitHub
description: Sync issues from a GitHub repository onto a Tale project board. Each scheduled run lists the repository's issues via the GitHub connector and upserts each one onto the board, keyed by a stable external reference ("owner/repo#number") so re-runs update the existing task instead of creating duplicates. Pull requests are skipped — GitHub's issues endpoint returns PRs alongside issues, and only real issues become tasks. The open/closed lifecycle is owned by GitHub (a closed issue moves its task to 'done'; reopening an issue pulls a terminal task back to 'backlog'), while everything in between is owned by local triage and is never clobbered by a sync. Configure `state: "all"` (the default) so closing an issue is reflected; narrow to `state: "open"` if you only want a one-way intake of active work. This workflow is the GitHub counterpart of the Google Drive / Gmail / Shopify sync automations: provider access lives in the `github` integration connector, and the sync logic lives here as data — there is no GitHub-specific backend code.

fr.name: Synchroniser les tickets depuis GitHub
fr.description: Importe les tickets d'un dépôt GitHub sur un tableau de projet Tale, en mettant à jour chacun via une référence externe stable et en ignorant les pull requests.

owner.description: GitHub repository owner (user or organization login), e.g. "tale-project".

projectId.description: Tale project ID whose board the issues sync onto. Copy from the project URL.

state.description: Which issues to sync: "all" (default), "open", or "closed". Use "all" so closing an issue moves its task to done.

labels.description: Optional comma-separated label filter (e.g. "bug,triage"). Leave empty to sync all issues.

config.description: The loop step throws on an empty items array (the throw isn't covered by continueOnError), so an empty issue list would otherwise abort the run. Route the empty case straight to done.
GitHub's issues endpoint returns pull requests too; PR objects carry a `pull_request` field that plain issues lack. Only real issues become tasks; PRs route straight back to the loop.
